argument.text: Let J=[r/2,3r/2] and take compact C from H003. M005 gives compact C×J, and M004 makes the continuous function e_t uniformly continuous there. By uniform continuity choose δ>0 such that any two points of C×J at distance less than δ have e_t-values differing by less than 1. The balls of radius δ/2 centered at points of C×J cover it; compactness gives a finite subcover with centers p₁,…,p_k. Hence |e_t(p)|≤1+max_i|e_t(p_i)| throughout C×J; choose this finite nonnegative bound K. The field e_t vanishes outside C. The set C is measurable and has finite Lebesgue measure. M008 gives integrability on C of the constant K; M009 gives integrability on ℝⁿ of b=K·1_C. For F(τ)(x)=e(x,τ) and F′(τ)(x)=e_t(x,τ), each F(τ) is strongly measurable by continuity; the support/integrability result gives F(r) integrable; F′(r) is continuous and strongly measurable. Smoothness gives the pointwise parameter derivative, and |F′(τ)(x)|≤b(x) for every x and τ∈J. M006's neighborhood, eventual strong measurability, base integrability, derivative measurability, integrable domination and pointwise derivative hypotheses are therefore satisfied. It yields that E is differentiable at r with E′(r)=∫e_t(x,r)dx. Since r was arbitrary this holds at every positive time.
